figures.use: A spec script's chance of a sale reads its genre's share of the year's deals (action and thriller lead recently; drama and comedy have fallen), and the market's size reads the year's total.

figures.finding: In 2012 the Scoggins Report counted 132 spec sales, with the thriller the most popular spec genre for the second year running; a ScriptMag analysis of those 132 put thrillers at 27%, action/adventure 22%, comedy 21%, sci-fi 11%, horror 10% and drama last at 8%.
figures.applies: US spec market, 2012, Jason Scoggins's tracker (a second tracker beside Go Into The Story, with a different count).
figures.use: A second count of the same market for cross-checking the 2012 genre shares; the game uses Go Into The Story's series as its main spec-market figure.

sources.said: 2012’s total number of spec sales - 132 - was exactly the same as 2011’s.
The most popular spec genre in 2012 was the Thriller, for the second year in a row.
So the sales included 27% thrillers, 22% action/adventure, and 21% comedies. Plus 11% sci-fi and 10% horror. Drama comes in dead last.

figures.finding: Of the writers, directors and top-billed stars of the 2,600 top-grossing US/Canada films of 2000-2025, roughly a quarter had family already in film or TV before they joined: stars 28%, directors 26%, writers 18%.

value.unit: share with a parent or close blood relative in film/TV before entry

figures.applies: Top ~100 US/Canada grossing films per year, 2000-2025; shares of people whose family background could be established.
figures.use: The share of lives born to a family in the business is drawn by role from these figures (an actor's family more often than a writer's), so the family trade is a weighted draw, not an even one.

sources.said: Of the people I studied, roughly a quarter had a family member already in the film or TV industry before they joined. Top-billed actors lead on 28%. Directors are close behind on 26%. Writers come out lower, on 18%
30% of top films have no nepo baby anywhere in their core team. 36% carry exactly one, 23% carry two, and 11% have three or more.

figures.finding: Directors with family in the business made their first feature younger (median 33 against 35), reached the top 100 faster (8 years against 10), went on to a second feature more often (72% against 66%) and had longer careers (median three features against two), but their films grossed no more (median $84m against $87m) and were rated no better.
figures.applies: Directors whose first feature came out 2000-2024 with at least 10,000 IMDb ratings (1,804 directors).
figures.use: A family in the business gives a director an earlier first chance and a better chance of a second after a flop (72% against 66%), and nothing to the film's gross or reviews.

sources.said: Connected directors get their first film made younger (a median age of 33 against 35), and those who eventually reached the top 100 climbed faster (a median of 8 years from first feature against 10). Most of all, they get more chances. 72% went on to a second feature against 66% of everyone else, and their median career is three features against two.
Films directed by industry-family directors have a median adjusted domestic gross of $84m, compared with $87m for films directed by everyone else.

figures.finding: Of 4,403 actors under 35 in US films of 2000-2025 whose family status could be confirmed, 28% (1,242) had at least one parent who worked in entertainment; of those, 60% had a parent in acting, 16% directing, 14% music, 9% producing, and 41% had two industry parents.

value.by_year: about 6-8% of young casts in the 2000s and 2010s, 16.6% by 2024 (as the report states)

figures.applies: Actors under 35 at release in US films 2000-2025 meeting a visibility criterion; a data company's own sample, which says it does not represent all working actors.
figures.use: Which trade an actor's industry parent had (acting most often) is drawn from these shares; a cross-check on Follows's 28% for stars.

sources.said: From 2000 to 2025, nepo babies made up 28% of confirmed young actors in U.S. movies, while 72% were non-nepo stars.
Directing was the second most common connection at 16%, followed by the music sector at 14% and producing at 9%.
Most nepo stars came from one-industry-parent households: 59% had one parent in entertainment, while 41% had two parents in the entertainment industry.
The confirmed-status sample included 4,403 actors under age 35, of whom 1,242 were confirmed nepo actors.

figures.finding: Gorji, Carney and Prakash (2020) find, on IMDb data for Hollywood show-business families, strong support that third-party network sponsorship benefits relatives' careers, more so for women, alongside the continuing importance of direct family preferment.

value.effect: sponsorship by family associates significantly benefits relatives' career performance; accentuated for women; direct preferment also matters

figures.applies: Hollywood movie industry, show-business family relatives (abstract only; the full text is paywalled).
figures.use: A family in the business works through the people the family knows (a contact who sponsors the player), which is how the game's contacts engine should carry it.

sources.said: We find strong support for our sponsorship hypotheses, but we also note the continuing importance of direct forms of family preferment in an industry characterized by single project organizations and boundaryless careers.

figures.finding: In UK film, TV, video, radio and photography, 12.4% of workers had working-class parents (NS-SEC 6-8) against 35% of the whole workforce, and 25.8% had parents in higher managerial and professional jobs (NS-SEC 1) against 13.7%; music, performing and visual art: 18.2% and 28.9%.

value.unit: share of workers by parents' NS-SEC

figures.applies: UK, Labour Force Survey (Oakley, Laurison, O'Brien and Friedman 2017), as tabled in Panic! 2018.
figures.use: The family's trade sets its class by NS-SEC, and a working-class family is about a third as common among the game's screen workers as in the population, which the background draw should reflect.

figures.finding: At the BFI Film Fund (2017-2022), applicants from middle-class backgrounds were more successful at the Development stage: 43% of middle-class writers succeeded against 25% of working-class writers, and producers 44% against 21%; only 4% of Development awards went to working-class producers.

value.applicants_managerial_professional_share: two thirds, against 37% of the workforce

figures.applies: UK, applicants to the BFI Film Fund (NETWORK, Development, Production strands), 2017-2022, class by parental occupation.
figures.use: Where the game models a UK public fund's decision, the applicant's class of origin moves the success rate by these published rates (the paper reports them; it does not claim class causes them).

sources.said: As seen in Table 4, for instance, 43% of middle class writers who apply for Development funds are successful, compared to 25% of working class writers.
Development Producer 44 40 21 Director 42 29 31 Writer 43 37 25
In total, only 4% of awards to the Development fund go to producers from working class backgrounds.
Overall, two thirds of applicants are from managerial/professional backgrounds, as compared with 37% of the total workforce from this background in 2022.

figures.finding: US family net worth in 2025 by the reference person's occupation (2025 dollars): managerial or professional median $295,300 (mean $1,893,300); technical, sales or services $150,500 ($567,600); other occupations $108,900 ($454,500); self-employed $574,600 ($3,520,100); working for someone else $156,000 ($684,600); all families $215,900 ($1,241,500).
figures.applies: United States, families, Survey of Consumer Finances 2025 (series 1989-2025 in the same table).
figures.use: A US family's means (money.means) is drawn around its trade's median net worth here, so a managerial family starts about twice as well off as a services family, and a self-employed one higher still.

figures.finding: Euro area household net wealth in 2023 by the reference person's work status: employee median €116,300 (mean €245,400), self-employed €327,000 (€792,900), retired €196,500 (€346,800), other not working €16,000 (€132,100); all households €140,100 (€312,000).
figures.applies: Euro area, HFCS 2023 wave (2021 wave in 2023 euros beside it); the HFCS statistical tables give work status only, not occupation.
figures.use: A euro-area family's means is drawn around its work status's median; the trade's occupation level is not published here, so the SCF's occupation ratios stand in, said so in the game.

sources.said: Net wealth also varies depending on the work status of the reference person. It is lowest when the reference person does not work and is not retired, increases for employees and the retired, and is highest among the self-employed.

figures.finding: In Great Britain (April 2020 to March 2022), 32% of adults in higher managerial and professional occupations lived in households worth £1 million or more against 5% in routine occupations; 19% of routine workers' households were worth under £20,000 against 2%.

value.unit: % of individuals by household total wealth band

figures.applies: Great Britain, adults 16+ not in full-time education, by their own NS-SEC (SOC 2020 from April 2020), Wealth and Assets Survey.
figures.use: A British family's means is drawn from its NS-SEC row's wealth bands, so the trade fixes the odds of each band rather than one number.

figures.finding: Spotlight (UK) asks that a performer's main photo be a recent head-and-shoulders shot, at least 500 by 500 pixels and 1MB to 40MB, with up to 15 photos free, and advises being prepared to change headshots every couple of years.

value.refresh: every couple of years (Spotlight's advice, not an enforced rule)

figures.applies: Spotlight performer profiles, UK and Ireland, as published November 2026.
figures.use: A headshot goes stale after about two years (Spotlight's own advice) or when the player's looks change; a stale or missing main photo lowers the chance a submission is called in.

sources.said: It should be a recent head and shoulders shot.
You can upload 15 Spotlight profile photos for free, but 4 or 5 excellent, well-chosen shots are much better.
At least 1MB and no more than 40MB
You should be prepared to change your headshots every couple of years and delete any photos that no longer represent you.
they should be an accurate representation of how you currently look.

figures.finding: Every submission on Casting Workbook and Casting Networks goes out under a photo from the profile (the submission's cover or primary photo); a free Actors Access account holds 2 headshots and a new Casting Networks account 2 photo credits.

figures.use: A life without a headshot can't submit for a part on these platforms (each submission is sent under a photo); the first headshot unlocks submissions.

sources.said: The final page is where you can choose which photo from your profile appears with your Submission (please note: this is just the cover photo of your submission, Casting is able to see your entire portfolio once submitted).
2 free headshots

value.sample: one spec of a current series or one original pilot
value.judged: blind, by WGAW showrunners and writer-producers

figures.use: A WGAW member who names one of these identities (or is 55 or over) may enter the Access Project; an honoree's script is read by showrunners at staffing season.

sources.said: Scripts will be considered in five categories: BIPOC writers Disabled writers Women writers Writers age 55 and over (as of November 8, 2021) LGBTQ+ writers

value.rule: limited to those who identify themselves as Indigenous
value.graton: proof of California-based tribal affiliation or lineal descendancy
value.women_directors_fellowship: Indigenous artists who identify as women and are endeavoring to direct a feature film

figures.use: Only a life whose ethnicity includes an Indigenous identity can apply to these; the Graton Fellowship also asks for the tribal paper.

figures.finding: The CAPE New Writers Fellowship develops Asian and Pacific Islander writers but its eligibility is open to writers over 18 of any race; applicants need a pilot, must not be currently staffed, and must be eligible to work in the US.

value.eligibility_identity: none: any race, color, sex, religion, national origin, disability or sexual orientation
value.work_permit: US employment eligibility, no visa sponsorship

figures.applies: US, CAPE (Coalition of Asian Pacifics in Entertainment), 2026-27 cycle.
figures.use: CAPE's door reads no ethnicity (anyone over 18 with US work papers and no current staff job may apply); its focus is mission, not a gate.

sources.said: Q: Do I have to be of Asian American or Pacific Islander heritage to apply? A: No. The CAPE New Writers Fellowship is open to writers over 18 years old of any race, color, sex, religion, national origin, disability or sexual orientation.
Applicants must not be currently staffed as a writer on an episodic program.
CAPE is unable to provide any type of Visa or work permit sponsorship or assistance – no exceptions.

figures.finding: Disney Entertainment Television's Writing Program (2027) requires US work eligibility and age 21 by 1 December 2026, two original live-action pilots and a resume, and names no identity; NBCUniversal's NBC TV Writers Program names lived experience (including racial and ethnic background, disability, LGBTQ+ and veterans) as its aim, and took eight writers in 2024-25; WBD Access describes its programme as for underrepresented, emerging writers.

figures.use: Disney's and NBC's doors read age, US work papers and the samples, not ethnicity; the game must not gate them on race, only list the aim where the programme states it.

sources.title: Spotlight, Everything You Need to Know About... Photos
sources.said: It should be a recent head and shoulders shot. … You can upload 15 Spotlight profile photos for free, but 4 or 5 excellent, well-chosen shots are much better. … At least 1MB and no more than 40MB

sources.title: Spotlight, 7 Headshot Tips from Casting Directors
sources.said: You should be prepared to change your headshots every couple of years and delete any photos that no longer represent you.

sources.title: Spotlight, How to Get the Perfect Headshot (29 Sep 2023)
sources.said: they should be an accurate representation of how you currently look.

sources.title: Casting Workbook Help, How Do I Submit To A Breakdown
sources.said: The final page is where you can choose which photo from your profile appears with your Submission (please note: this is just the cover photo of your submission, Casting is able to see your entire portfolio once submitted).

sources.title: Breakdown Services FAQ
sources.said: 2 free headshots … For $68/year or $9.99/month your Actors Access PLUS membership includes all the features of a free Actors Access account

sources.title: Casting Networks Support, TALENT REPRESENTATIVE: What tips can I share with my talent
sources.said: All new accounts receive 2 free photo credits, 1 video, and 1 audio.

sources.title: Casting Networks Support, TALENT REPRESENTATIVES: How do I customize my submissions?
sources.said: You can either choose an existing photo from your talent's profile to be the primary photo for the submission, or you can upload a brand new one just for this submission.

sources.title: WGA West, TV Writers Access Project Call for Submissions (Connect, 12 Nov 2021)
sources.said: Scripts will be considered in five categories: BIPOC writers Disabled writers Women writers Writers age 55 and over (as of November 8, 2021) LGBTQ+ writers … Qualifying WGAW members can submit one piece of literary material

sources.title: Sundance Institute, Indigenous Program
sources.said: Our program strives to uplift the voices of Indigenous artists and our opportunities are limited to those who identify themselves as Indigenous. … Indigenous artists who are from a California-based tribe and can provide proof of tribal affiliation or lineal descendancy. … This opportunity is open to U.S.-based and international Indigenous artists who identify as women and are endeavoring to direct a feature film.

sources.title: CAPE, New Writers Fellowship FAQ
sources.said: Q: Do I have to be of Asian American or Pacific Islander heritage to apply? A: No. The CAPE New Writers Fellowship is open to writers over 18 years old of any race, color, sex, religion, national origin, disability or sexual orientation. … CAPE is unable to provide any type of Visa or work permit sponsorship or assistance – no exceptions.

sources.title: CAPE New Writers Fellowship
sources.said: Applicants must not be currently staffed as a writer on an episodic program.

sources.title: Disney Entertainment Television, Writing Program Application 2027
sources.said: Applicants must be able to legally work in the United States and be at least twenty-one (21) years of age by December 1, 2026.

sources.title: NBCUniversal, NBCU Launch Welcomes 2024-25 Class of NBC TV Writers Program
sources.said: This includes talent from various socio-economic backgrounds, geographic locations, racial and ethnic backgrounds, people with disabilities, the LGBTQ+ community and veterans, among other communities. … Meet the Eight New Members of the NBC TV Writers Program
